The chemical formula of table salt is **NaCl**.

It consists of:
- **Na** — sodium (a metal)
- **Cl** — chlorine (a nonmetal)

These two elements bond together **ionically**: sodium loses one electron to become a positively charged ion (Na⁺), and chlorine gains that electron to become a negatively charged ion (Cl⁻). The opposite charges attract, forming a crystal lattice structure rather than discrete molecules.

This is why table salt is more precisely called **sodium chloride**, and in its solid form it exists as a repeating three-dimensional grid of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻
